title: SymDiag: Explainable Diagnosis for LLM Reasoning via Neuro-Symbolic Verification

problem.claim: LLM chains-of-thought can be unfaithful even when final answers are correct.

gap.claim: Existing verification signals provide limited diagnosis of where multi-step reasoning fails or rely on subjective critiques.

contributions.claim: SymDiag reframes reasoning verification as structured failure diagnosis using a neuro-symbolic framework.
SymDiag translates natural-language chains-of-thought into symbolic constraints and performs step-level satisfiability and entailment checks.
A Self-Auditor uses dual symbolic encoding consistency checks to distinguish TranslationError from ReasoningError.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across diverse mathematical, logical, scientific, and general reasoning benchmarks, SymDiag improves detection of unfaithful reasoning.
SymDiag provides more effective feedback for multi-round reasoning repair than outcome-only verification and LLM-based judging.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM chains-of-thought may be unfaithful despite correct final answers.
Existing verification signals do not adequately diagnose failures in multi-step derivations.
SymDiag performs symbolic, step-level checks to localize failures and generate diagnostic evidence.
Apparent logic violations may result from reasoning defects or translation noise.
A Self-Auditor separates translation and reasoning errors, and the authors report improved diagnosis and repair feedback across benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Step-level symbolic checks can produce localized failure information and diagnostic artifacts such as counterexamples and missing-premise indicators.

interpretation.claim: Verification may be more useful for debugging when it explains a failure rather than only judging the final outcome.

application.claim: Design reasoning-monitoring systems to expose intermediate failure locations and evidence.

exception.claim: Apparent symbolic violations may reflect translation noise rather than genuine reasoning defects.

source_observation.claim: Dual symbolic encoding consistency checks are used to distinguish TranslationError from ReasoningError.

interpretation.claim: Independent or redundant representations can help separate upstream interpretation errors from downstream reasoning errors.

application.claim: Use representation-consistency checks when translating neural reasoning into structured forms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the encodings, consistency procedure, or its behavior under different translation failures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark names, datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the symbolic encodings, implementation details, or diagnostic evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
